findings.title: Redis OSS 2.8.24 is past end of life
findings.description:
RedisReplicationGroup (Elasticache-snapshot.yaml) runs engine redis, EngineVersion 2.8.24 (ElastiCache/Elasticache-snapshot.yaml:147), parameter group family redis2.8 (ElastiCache/Elasticache-snapshot.yaml:117). Past end of life since 2023-01-13. Not eligible for Extended Support. AWS recommends 6.2 or higher. Confirm the Valkey upgrade path. Redis OSS 2.x is not enrolled in Extended Support, so it is not paying Extended Support; it receives no fixes or security patches. The AWS docs do not state whether a direct cross-engine upgrade from 2.8.24 to Valkey is allowed: confirm with describe-cache-engine-versions or AWS Support before planning a single-step upgrade. Upgrades from versions older than 5.0.6 pause writes for 30-60 seconds. Risk score 3 (Medium): version older than 5.0.6 (+2), no test or staging environment found (+1). Topology: NumCacheClusters 2 with AutomaticFailoverEnabled true (no single-node penalty). Recommended: Valkey 9.1 (rule 3, no Redis client code in the repository fails the client check). Alternatives: Valkey 8.2, Valkey 7.2 (in-place rollback to Redis OSS 7.1), Redis OSS 7.1 (avoids the Valkey TLS requirement). Never Redis OSS 6.x. Parameter group family must move to valkey9 (or the chosen target family).

findings.title: In-transit encryption is not set (required for a Valkey replication group)
findings.description: RedisReplicationGroup (Elasticache-snapshot.yaml) does not set TransitEncryptionEnabled. The CloudFormation docs require TransitEncryptionEnabled when creating a Valkey replication group and cfn-lint rejects a Valkey replication group without it. Turning on TLS changes how every client connects. Proposed manual change: enable TLS (TransitEncryptionMode: preferred first, then required) and move clients to TLS, or choose Redis OSS 7.1 (target C). Not changed automatically.

findings.title: Live data, AWS Health and Trusted Advisor not used (live_access=off)
findings.description: live_access=off was set, so no AWS API was called: no caller identity, AWS Health events, Trusted Advisor checks, live clusters or DescribeCacheEngineVersions were read. Status is computed from AWS documentation and the run date; drift was not checked; target versions (Valkey 9.1, 8.2) come from the AWS docs and must be confirmed in the Region. live_data=unavailable is set in every plan block.

findings.title: No Redis client application code found
findings.description: No Redis client library or Redis command usage was found (no package manifests with Redis clients, no docker-compose/Helm Redis images, no Lua, INFO parsing or hard-coded node IPs). ElastiCache/elastic-code.js is a CloudFormation custom resource that calls the ElastiCache control-plane API (ModifyReplicationGroup) through aws-sdk; it does not connect to Redis and is not affected by the engine change. Consumers of this template outside the repository were not visible.
